p1s.summary: The melting-temperature conditions the Methods print — "nearest-neighbour values for an unmodified DNA:RNA hybrid at 250 nM strand" — are correct at the pin and read by no instrument. Nothing binds 250 to junction-aso-thermo.json, so a drift to 100 nM or 1 uM would ship green.
p1s.evidence: Correct at the pin: research/modalities/junction-aso-thermo.json `conditions` = {"temperature_k": 310.15, "strand_conc_nm": 250.0, "delta_g_units": "kcal/mol"}, and `parameters.table` = Bio.SeqUtils.MeltingTemp.R_DNA_NN1 with `pmid` 7545436, the reference the sentence cites (ref 16). Coverage: `git grep -l` at the pin for "nM strand" returns only the journal article, the extended report's claim-audit manifest/verdicts and the SI — no test and no linter. Of the 89 entries in research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json, exactly 18 name fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.md in `must_appear_in`, and none of them is a thermo figure (ids enumerated in my log). `grep -rn 'strand_conc\|250 nM\|nM strand'` over research/manuscripts/tests/*.py returns nothing.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Re-running junction_aso_thermo.py at a different strand concentration, or an editorial pass normalising "250 nM" to another value, changes the condition under which every Tm in the paper and both Table 1 dTm floors were computed. No guard reads the number, so the sentence and the artifact would silently disagree.

p1s.summary: The sentence that makes the dTm separation a FLOOR — "the fusion duplex pairs all ten locked residues where each parent pairs five" — carries two numbers no instrument reads. It is a one-sided bound, the exact class this repository has already shipped reversed once.
p1s.evidence: Correct at the pin: research/modalities/junction-aso-thermo.json the field keyed `⚠_lna_not_modelled` states "the fusion duplex pairs all TEN LNA residues while each parent duplex pairs exactly FIVE, for every design by construction"; the geometry that forces it is 5-6-5 with the breakpoint inside the gap (aso-parent-gap-pairing.json `method`: oligo_len 16, wing 5, gap_positions_0based [5,10]). Coverage: `git grep -l 'ten locked residues'` at the pin returns the journal article, the claim-audit pair, research/manuscripts/aso_journal_tables.py (as a docstring, lines 159-164, not an assertion), aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json and junction_aso_thermo.py — no test file. None of the 18 journal-article entries in pinned-figures.json covers it. The same artifact's own header records that a neighbouring field "previously said the opposite, that LNA 'compresses ddG' and the value is an UPPER bound", so a reversed one-sided bound is a realised failure mode here, and test_journal_article_numbers.py::test_the_ddg_separations... exists because of it — but it guards the kcal/mol sentence, not this one.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Swapping ten and five, or changing "where each parent pairs five" to "at least five", turns a floor into a ceiling and makes the reported fusion-versus-parent separation read as more margin than was computed. Both numerals and the direction word would stay green.

p1s.summary: "which admits five per junction" is deliberately left unbound by the guard that binds the rest of that sentence — but the number IS in a committed artifact, so the gap is closable rather than unbindable, and the reason recorded for leaving it open reads the wrong file.
p1s.evidence: The claim is correct at the pin: research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json `geometries[0]` (5-6-5, oligo_len 16) records `junction_spanning_registers_per_seam` = 5, and nr4a3-fusion-junction-atlas.json carries `n_tiled` == 5 on all 38 panels (I counted: Counter({5: 38}), summing to the 190 designs). research/manuscripts/tests/test_journal_article_numbers.py::test_the_tiled_geometry_the_methods_state_is_the_one_the_canonical_file_carries states in its docstring: "WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT BIND is the sentence's 'which admits five per junction'. The artifact carries 2-5 designs per junction at this geometry". That 2-5 spread is a property of fusion-junction-aso-sequences.csv, which keys rows to 43 junctions across three geometries and both acceptor arms; the 38-junction 5-6-5 panel the sentence is about is flat five.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: An edit to "which admits seven per junction" (the 5-8-5 figure, which the same artifact carries) or to any other count passes every gate, because the guard that reads this sentence asserts the geometry string, the 16-mer and the six-nucleotide gap and explicitly skips the register count.

p2s.summary: "At 5-10-5 pairing the whole gap already demands ten base pairs, more than the seven-to-ten the enzyme is reported to need" — ten is the TOP of the cited seven-to-ten range, not more than it. The floor conclusion survives on the range's lower end and nothing downstream moves, but the comparative as printed is not exact.
p2s.evidence: The paper's own statement of the requirement, in the Introduction: "Its length requirement is reported as a DNA gap of at least six nucleotides, with seven to ten the working range" (ref 13, PMID 24981949). At 5-10-5 the catalytic gap is ten nucleotides, so pairing it in full is exactly ten paired bases: research/modalities/aso-gap-length-tradeoff.json `geometries[2].mature_parent_whole_gap_duplex` has n_with_any_gap_pairing_window == n_at_or_above_min_duplex_bp == 87, i.e. the two coincide. Ten is therefore equal to the top of [7,10], not above it. What makes the count a floor is the LOWER end: a parent pairing only seven, eight or nine gap nucleotides could still license cleavage and is uncounted. Wording that would be exact and no longer: 'more than the seven the enzyme is reported to need at least'.

p2s.summary: "8 designs carry a fully paired sixteen-base-pair off-target duplex and 45 one inside 2 kcal/mol of their own" — the 45 CONTAINS the 8, and the sentence does not say so where two neighbouring sentences flag exactly this hazard for other counts.
p2s.evidence: Recomputed from research/modalities/aso-offtarget-duplex-energy.json `designs[]`: the 8 designs with max_run_len_hybridisable == 16 all have min_ddg_gap_paired == 0.000 (ddG is 0 by construction for a whole-oligo run), and every one of them also has n_gap_paired_within_2_kcal > 0, so {the 8} is a strict subset of {the 45} (checked: all 8 in the 45). The paper flags nesting explicitly twice nearby — "As a union rather than a sum the two screens condemn 93 of the 190" and "Neither restates the other, and their counts may not be added" — so a reader trained by those sentences may read 8 and 45 as disjoint and total 53. Both numerals are correct and both are pinned (pinned-figures.json ids aso_energy_designs_with_a_fully_paired_offtarget and aso_energy_designs_within_2_kcal).

p2s.summary: "reported doubling times of five to six days" rounds a source value that is above six.
p2s.evidence: research/manuscripts/aso/fusion-junction-aso-claim-audit-verdicts.json quotes PMID 36316541 verbatim: "a doubling time of 5.09 days for [USZ20-EMC1] and 6.05 days for [USZ22-EMC2]". 6.05 rounds to 6 at one significant figure, so the printed bracket is right to the precision it states and slightly narrower than the source at its upper end. research/manuscripts/tests/test_the_numbered_claims_no_instrument_read.py::test_the_models_doubling_times_bracket_what_the_paper_rounds_them_to already reads both values against the prose, so this is disclosed, not unwatched.
